_about: Hand-reviewed E4 scope decisions (2026-09-23), read by scripts/remediation/mechanical/scope.py. Every quote must appear verbatim in the site's live description or the planner refuses the decision. Rule (a) - T11/out-of-window - retires by default; an entry here can only turn that into 'pending', and only with a quote that dates part of the site inside the E3 window. Rule (b) - T11/undecidable-date - is 'pending' by default; an entry retires it only with a quote that places it outside the window, or keeps a Museum row by the E3 museum rule. Rule (d) - T11/museum-past-cutoff - has no default: every row needs an entry (plan section 8.2).

decisions.name: Damascus Gate
decisions.quote: Beneath it lies a Roman-era triumphal gate with three arched openings, dating to c. 135 AD
decisions.note: Phase 3 wrote period_start 1 -> 1537 (the Ottoman gate); the site's own description dates the Roman gate beneath it to c. 135 AD, inside the window. A period_start question before a scope one.

decisions.name: Church of the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul, Ras
decisions.quote: Founded in the 4th century during Roman rule
decisions.note: Phase 3 wrote period_start 1 -> 820; the site's own description says it was founded in the 4th century, inside the window.

decisions.name: Foso e Interior Citadelle De Victoria
decisions.quote: Archaeological evidence shows habitation since the Bronze Age, with the site believed to have served as the acropolis of the Punic-Roman city of Gaulos
decisions.note: Phase 3 wrote period_start -3000 -> 1500 (the medieval castle); the description attests Bronze Age and Punic-Roman use. The remaining-map note that this write may be wrong stands.

decisions.name: Gårdstånga
decisions.quote: The site features a Bronze Age burial mound (gravhog)
decisions.note: Phase 3 wrote period_start -4500 -> 900 (the settlement); the row's site_type is Mound/tumulus and its own description dates the mound to the Bronze Age.

decisions.name: Panamá Viejo
decisions.quote: Archaeological excavations have uncovered evidence of pre-Columbian Cuevan peoples, demonstrating over 700 years of pre-Hispanic occupation before European contact
decisions.note: Phase 3 wrote period_start 1000 -> 1519 (the Spanish foundation); the description attests pre-Columbian occupation, inside the Americas window.

decisions.name: Skopje Aqueduct
decisions.quote: theories attribute it to Roman times (1st century AD, supplying the settlement of Scupi)
decisions.note: Phase 3 wrote period_start 1 -> 1600; the description calls the construction date debated between Roman, Byzantine and Ottoman.

decisions.name: Keno Daas Rock Carvings
decisions.quote: The region's Buddhist rock art, which peaked between the 5th and 8th centuries AD
decisions.note: period_start 600 (pre-remediation); the description's range starts in the 5th century, inside the window.

decisions.name: Chacamarca Historic Sanctuary
decisions.quote: The sanctuary also protects archaeological remains of the Pumpush culture, an ancient highland civilization of the Bombon Plateau
decisions.note: period_start 1974 is the protected area's creation; the description names pre-Columbian remains. Plan section 8.2 lists it among the rows that are not museums.

decisions.name: Delphi Archaeological Museum
decisions.quote: The collection spans from the Late Helladic (Mycenean) period to the early Byzantine era
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1903 is the founding year.

decisions.name: Ephesus Archaeological Museum
decisions.quote: Its most celebrated exhibit is the ancient statue of the Greek Goddess Artemis
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1964 is the founding year.

decisions.name: Grenoble Archaeological Museum
decisions.quote: The site preserves layers from a 4th-century Gallo-Roman necropolis
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1846 is not the date of the collection.

decisions.name: Jadar Museum
decisions.quote: Notable exhibits include Roman-era Illyrian artifacts
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1984 is not the date of the collection.

decisions.name: Kharakhorum Museum
decisions.quote: It houses 3,128 artifacts spanning from the Upper Palaeolithic to the 14th century
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 2007 is the building's start.

decisions.name: Maria Reiche Museum
decisions.quote: the house was converted into a museum displaying her research materials, maps, blueprints, and archaeological finds
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: the museum of the Nazca Lines research displays archaeological finds; period_start 1994 is not the date of the collection.

decisions.name: Museo Campano
decisions.quote: houses an extensive collection of matres matutae ritual statues from the ancient Roman site of Capua antica
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1869 is the founding year.

decisions.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
decisions.quote: The museum houses eleven anthropology galleries covering pre-Columbian civilizations including Teotihuacan
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1964 is the inauguration year.

decisions.name: Museo Regional de Antropologia Carlos Pellier
decisions.quote: The collection includes monumental Olmec stone sculptures from La Venta
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1980 is the opening year.

decisions.name: Museo Regional de Campeche
decisions.quote: This two-story building displays a pre-Hispanic collection from the Gulf and Central Highlands regions
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1986 is the opening year.

decisions.name: Museo de Antropologia de Xalapa
decisions.quote: The museum houses artifacts from Mesoamerican Gulf Coast cultures including the Olmec, Totonac, and Huastec
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1937 is the founding year.

decisions.name: Museo de la Arquitectura Maya
decisions.quote: The collection showcases architectural elements from four regional Maya styles
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 2005 is the reopening year.

decisions.name: Mérida Anthropological Museum
decisions.quote: The permanent collection spans from the pre-Classic to the late post-Classic Maya period
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1959 is not the date of the collection.

decisions.name: Pfahlbaumuseum Unteruhldingen
decisions.quote: featuring reconstructions of Neolithic and Bronze Age stilt houses
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits (reconstructed) ancient material; period_start 1922 is the founding year.

decisions.name: The Salisbury Museum
decisions.quote: including prehistoric material from Stonehenge
decisions.note: E3 museum rule: exhibits ancient material; period_start 1860 is the founding year.

decisions.name: Groß Raden Archaeological Open Air Museum
decisions.quote: uncovered remains of a Slavic settlement dating to the 9th and 10th centuries
decisions.note: Plan section 8.2: one of the 3 Museum rows that leave (Slavic settlement and temple, 9th/10th century). Phase 3 wrote period_start 1 -> 800.

decisions.name: Khushuu Tsaidam Museum
decisions.quote: dedicated to the 8th-century Orkhon inscriptions of the Gokturk Empire
decisions.note: Plan section 8.2: one of the 3 Museum rows that leave (Gokturk Orkhon stelae, 8th century).

decisions.name: King Richard III Visitor Centre
decisions.quote: where Richard III was buried in 1485
decisions.note: Plan section 8.2: one of the 3 Museum rows that leave (the 1485 grave of Richard III).

decisions.name: Bosnian Pyramid of Love
decisions.quote: The site has no verified archaeological significance.
decisions.note: A natural hill claimed as a pyramid since 2005; the 2026-09-19 assessment left the three Bosnian 'pyramids' to the owner. Not dated by any source, so not retired by rule (b).

decisions.name: Bosnian Pyramid of the Moon
decisions.quote: Excavations revealed only cracked sandstone plates separated by silt and clay layers -- consistent with natural geology, not construction.
decisions.note: As the Pyramid of Love: an owner decision, not a date.

decisions.name: Bosnian Pyramid of the Sun
decisions.quote: Geologists identify it as a natural flatiron formation.
decisions.note: As the Pyramid of Love: an owner decision. The only human structure the description names is the medieval royal fortress of Visoki.

decisions.name: Kamennyy Gorod
decisions.quote: A Megalithic site and protected nature reserve.
decisions.note: No source_url and no date anywhere in the row: nothing places it outside the window.

decisions.name: Leptis Magna Museum
decisions.quote: It contains evidence of people of different origins that once inhabited the city of Leptis Magna, including Berber, Punic, Phoenicians and Romans.
decisions.note: Undated Museum row: the E3 museum rule keeps it - it exhibits ancient material.

decisions.name: Mookambika Wildlife Sanctuary Kodachadri
decisions.quote: notified in 1974 and later expanded
decisions.note: Its own source describes a wildlife sanctuary created in 1974 and names no ancient site; the 2026-09-19 assessment listed it among the clear exclusions. site_type holds the marker 'suspect_modern'.

decisions.name: Northern Avenue Petroglyph Site
decisions.quote: the site served as a ceremonial site and animal facility in prehistory
decisions.note: Its own source places it in prehistory, inside the Americas window: only the date field is missing.

decisions.name: Popping Stone
decisions.quote: centered on the legend that Sir Walter Scott proposed to Charlotte Carpenter at this location in 1797
decisions.note: Natural boulders whose only human history in the source is the 1797 legend; the 2026-09-19 assessment listed it among the clear exclusions.

decisions.name: Prebreza
decisions.quote: The Prebreza Paleontological site is regarded an important European Mammalian site of the Middle Miocene.
decisions.note: A village with a Miocene paleontological site: a subject-scope question (not archaeology), not a date past the cutoff.

decisions.name: Rocks of Saskatchewan
decisions.quote: Very little is known about these rocks.
decisions.note: Nothing in the row dates it.

decisions.name: Singing Stones of Brittany
decisions.quote: The phenomenon is due to the rock's mineral composition and density
decisions.note: A natural phenomenon: a subject-scope question, not a date past the cutoff.

decisions.name: Situs Megalit Tebing Tinggi
decisions.quote: Part of the Pasemah highlands megalithic tradition dating approximately 2,000-3,000 years ago
decisions.note: Its own source places it inside the window: only the date field is missing.

decisions.name: Temple of Lemminkäinen
decisions.quote: According to Bock, the entrance was sealed in 987 when Christianity arrived in Uusimaa
decisions.note: The only date is the Bock saga's sealing of the cave, not its use; nothing places the site outside the window.

decisions.name: The Davidson Center
decisions.quote: The site spans approximately 5,000 years of history from the Canaanite Bronze Age through the Second Temple period.
decisions.note: Undated Museum row: the E3 museum rule keeps it - it exhibits ancient material.

decisions.name: Yonaguni Monument
decisions.quote: Neither the Japanese Agency for Cultural Affairs nor Okinawa Prefecture recognises it as a cultural artifact.
decisions.note: Natural or man-made is disputed and no source dates it: a subject-scope question.
